question.problem: Find an expression for the height $h$ of a cylinder in terms of its volume $V$ given that the ratio of the radius of the base to the height of the cylinder is $\frac{1}{3}.$
question.worked_solution:
Using the fact that the ratio of the radius $r$ of the base to the height $h$ is $\frac{1}{3},$ we have that

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{r}{h} & =\frac{1}{3}.\end{aligned}
$$

Our goal is to express $h$ in terms of $V.$ Therefore, we need to isolate $r$ in the above equation, which we do using cross-multiplication:

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{r}{h} & =\frac{1}{3} \\ 3r & =h \\ r & =\frac{h}{3}\end{aligned}
$$

The volume of a cylinder with radius $r$ and height $h$ is given by

$$
V=\pi {r}^{2}h.
$$

Therefore, substituting $r=\frac{h}{3}$ into the formula, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}V & =\pi {r}^{2}h \\ V & =\pi {(\frac{h}{3})}^{2}\cdot h \\ V & =\pi \cdot \frac{{h}^{2}}{9}\cdot h \\ V & =\frac{\pi {h}^{3}}{9} \\ {h}^{3} & =\frac{9V}{\pi } \\ h & =\sqrt[3]{\frac{9V}{\pi }}.\end{aligned}
$$
